# Facets sample vault

This small vault contains ordinary Markdown notes and a sparse K-Plex configuration. It includes no executable plugin or remote loader. Use the matching reviewed K-Plex build in a disposable vault; opening these examples is not an installation or permission to deploy to a personal vault.

1. Open Start here and K-Plex.
2. Select Views and lenses, then Canvas view: Facets.
3. Choose ARC, PARA, Wu Xing, GTD, eACCESS, Sensemaking, Publishing, Map roles or the custom State preset. Select Info beside the preset cog for its Help.
4. Follow Metal perspective and compare the five relative Wu Xing explanations.
5. Select a category through the note action or drop a note into a category; review the native preview before assigning. Undo is guarded against later edits.

The example notes cover all eight built-in presets and the custom State definition. Sensemaking combines explicit `approach`/`mode`; Map roles uses `map-role`. Ready for review demonstrates the built-in Publishing review stage, which intentionally remains Unassigned in the older four-category State example. Unassigned and Conflicting examples stay reachable. Normal note-to-note connectors come from children metadata and existing links. Solid generating and dashed regulating guides are decorative model explanations.

ARC (Add/Relate/Communicate) replaces the uncustomized ACE example; explicit saved ACE definitions retain their original facts. The eight presets are editable local examples, not official workflow engines or inferred importance scores. Try horizontal ARC, vertical Publishing, four-quadrant Sensemaking and concentric Map roles. See docs/FACETS.md in the source repository for details and attribution. Portable preset/lens examples live separately under tests/fixtures/portable-presets and must be previewed before importing.

To use this as a separate sample vault, install the matching plugin by its normal process; binaries are intentionally absent. Do not copy these settings over an existing vault. For repository validation the authorized disposable Small environment receives test-owned copies under a unique folder and is restored afterward.
